products.name: STOPit
products.note: Verified in the research for The AI Ready School. AI features: not verified. Use: Anonymous reporting app and hotline. Who: Students, staff. Student age: Students through school license. Privacy: Signed California student data privacy agreement (Westside Union SD, 2019) in the SDPC registry. Price: About $1 per student per year (Carroll ISD, Texas); some state programs, insurers, and co-ops fund it.

reading.body:
STOPit is an anonymous school reporting app priced at about $1 per student per year, and its AI features are not verified.

The product is a reporting channel, not a computing system. It runs on a mobile app, a website, and a phone hotline, and it is bought under a school license that covers students and staff. The only price in the record, roughly a dollar per student per year from Carroll ISD in Texas, puts a full district's coverage in the low tens of thousands of dollars. Some state programs, insurers, and co-ops pay instead of the district.

The one privacy fact in the record is a signed California student data privacy agreement from 2019, tied to Westside Union SD and listed in the SDPC registry. That is a contract about handling student data, not evidence of AI capability. The listing places STOPit under education and research AI, but the record states plainly that AI features are not verified, so the category label should not be read as a description of what the software does.

What the data does not cover matters here. There is no litigation, no SEC filing, no patent, and no MCP server in the record. There is no information about where the service is hosted, how much compute it uses, or what data center or power arrangements sit behind it. For a question about the grid or about AI scaling, this record is close to silent. It documents a cheap, widely deployed school safety tool with an unverified AI label, and nothing more.

profile_text.body:
STOPit Solutions describes itself as providing anonymous incident reporting and safety technology for the modern workplace through a mobile app, a web interface, and a phone hotline. The company says it works with more than 8,000 organizations nationwide to help protect their physical, social, and emotional well-being.

Its tracked product is STOPit, an anonymous reporting app and hotline used by students and staff, with student use covered through school licenses. The product carries a signed California student data privacy agreement with Westside Union SD from 2019 in the SDPC registry. Pricing is about $1 per student per year, as recorded for Carroll ISD in Texas, and some state programs, insurers, and co-ops fund it. AI features for the product have not been verified.

The company is also listed under the name Lightspeed Systems (StopIt). No lawsuits, MCP servers, or other filings are recorded for it.
